The 2.5x boost pays you back faster
Boost until you are paid back
Payout in one period (ETB), net profit ETB 100,000
Pool = 20% of ETB 100,000 = ETB 20,000. Your part = your shares / 2,000. Illustration, not a forecast.

Worked example: net profit ETB 100,000, pool ETB 20,000. A holder of 100 shares owns 5% of the pool: ETB 1,000 at the standard rate, ETB 2,500 while boosted. Once they have received back what they paid, the boost ends and they continue at the standard rate. Rule of thumb: 100 shares is 2.5% of net profit while boosted and 1% after payback.

A holder of 100 shares: ETB per period at ETB 100,000 net profit
With only Stage 1 sold, a 100-share holder earns ETB 7,500 (2,500 + 5,000). Stated in the Agreement. Illustration, not a promise.

This is the reward for being early, and it is written into the Agreement (draft clause on Unsold Profit Shares) and on the deal sheet. Example: net profit ETB 100,000, 400 of 2,000 shares sold. Unsold amount = 20,000 x 1,600/2,000 x 2.5 = 40,000. Half (20,000) is shared among the holders. A holder of 100 of the 400 sold shares receives 5,000 on top of the 2,500 ordinary boosted share: 7,500 in total. At 1,000 sold the bonus falls to 1,250; at 2,000 sold it is zero. The raise in three stages: the price rises as we prove it
Early investors take the most risk and pay the lowest price. A share is a profit-share right, not company ownership.
The investor pool: 2,000 shares = 20% of net profit

Stage 1 is open now and the cheapest: ETB 1,000 a share, 400 shares, ETB 400,000. Stage 2 (600 shares at ETB 1,500) opens when the platform reaches 400 trips a day. Stage 3 (1,000 shares at ETB 2,000) opens at 1,000 trips a day. The pool is 2,000 shares, which is 20% of net profit in total. Every share earns the same slice of profit, so a later investor pays more for the same slice. That is the reward for early risk. Repeat: profit-share rights, not company ownership.

Explain why: paying profit out while still buying growth would starve the launch. The launch ends at most 90 days after it starts (60 days at 0% commission for new drivers, then 30 days at 2%), or earlier when the 4-week average reaches 150 trips a day. The platform is built so that this rule is set in one place and shown identically to investors in the deal sheet, the pitch and the portal.
